title: 2.4 Consequences of Climate Change
description: Warming trends, precipitation shifts, sea level rise, polar change and ecosystem impacts. Hard level.

questions.question: How does the albedo feedback involving boreal forests and tundra work?
options: Dark forests absorb more sunlight than snow, accelerating warming
Forces that originate outside the Earth, mainly in the atmosphere
An increase in desert conditions from overgrazing and cultivation
The North American Plate includes western North Atlantic seafloor
questions.correctAnswer: Dark forests absorb more sunlight than snow, accelerating warming

questions.question: Why might Antarctica gain snow while still losing ice overall?
options: Dark forests absorb more sunlight than snow, accelerating warming
Orbital variations help initiate glacial and interglacial periods
Warmer air holds more snow inland while coastal melting increases
Forces that originate outside the Earth, mainly in the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: Warmer air holds more snow inland while coastal melting increases

questions.question: How does saltwater intrusion affect coastal groundwater supplies?
options: Rising seas push salt into freshwater aquifers
It will return exactly to preindustrial levels
The Atlantic Ocean once covered all continents
It increases groundwater temperature only
questions.correctAnswer: Rising seas push salt into freshwater aquifers

questions.question: How do climate-driven changes in species distribution affect human well-being?
options: Ocean basins can expand or shrink over geologic time
Climate is measured in hours; weather over centuries
Through emerging diseases and changes in food supply
Rain falls in heavier spells with longer dry periods
questions.correctAnswer: Through emerging diseases and changes in food supply

questions.question: Why might higher latitudes benefit initially from warming?
options: It included ministers as well as scientists
It lies entirely in the Southern Hemisphere
Continental crust is denser than the mantle
Longer growing seasons and earlier snowmelt
questions.correctAnswer: Longer growing seasons and earlier snowmelt

questions.question: What limits the carbon dioxide fertilization effect?
options: One region represents the whole planet perfectly
Shortages of water, nitrogen and other nutrients
Continental crust is buoyant and resists sinking
The reptile evolved separately on each continent
questions.correctAnswer: Shortages of water, nitrogen and other nutrients

questions.question: How does faster decomposition of soil organic matter amplify warming?
options: There was a discernible human influence on global climate
They trap heat and raise air temperatures near the ground
It releases additional carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
By adding greenhouse gases and aerosols to the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: It releases additional carbon dioxide into the atmosphere

questions.question: Which regions are projected to face decreasing crop yields?
options: The bending of rock layers due to sideways earth movements
Shock waves released by shifting rock during an earthquake
It reduces emissions through modern efficient technologies
Tropical regions where many developing nations are located
questions.correctAnswer: Tropical regions where many developing nations are located

questions.question: What explains the projected increase in wildfires in high-latitude forests?
options: More frequent dry spells in forested areas
Human influence will continue to change it
Land between two faults that has sunk down
More frequent rainfall in forests
questions.correctAnswer: More frequent dry spells in forested areas

questions.question: Why is a single warm year insufficient to demonstrate global warming?
options: Warming is small in any year and significant only over decades
A fracture forms and one limb is pushed forward over the other
It shows a long-term rise in global land and ocean temperature
Faster decomposition releases more carbon dioxide into the air
questions.correctAnswer: Warming is small in any year and significant only over decades
